cosy-lesson.title: Culture Helps Your Body Stay Younger

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Museum – a building in which objects of historical, scientific, artistic, or cultural interest are stored and exhibited.

p.em: Example: I love to visit the history museum on rainy Sunday afternoons.

cosy-blockquote.p: Theater – a building or outdoor area in which plays and other dramatic performances are given.

p.em: Example: We bought tickets to see a famous comedy play at the local theater.

cosy-blockquote.p: Young ≠ Old – having lived or existed for only a short time ≠ having lived for a long time; far advanced in the life span.

p.em: Example: Our young daughter loves to run around, while our old dog prefers to sleep near the fireplace.

cosy-blockquote.p: Culture – the arts, music, and traditions shared by a group of people.

p.em: Example: Learning about the local culture makes traveling much more interesting.

cosy-blockquote.p: Activity – a thing that a person or group does or has done.

p.em: Example: Going for a bike ride is a very healthy weekend activity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Stress – a state of mental or emotional strain or tension resulting from adverse or demanding circumstances.

p.em: Example: Listening to classical music is a great way to reduce daily stress.

cosy-blockquote.p: Reduce – make smaller or less in amount, degree, or size.

p.em: Example: Regular physical exercise can help reduce high blood pressure.

cosy-blockquote.p: Trip – a short journey or visit to a place.

p.em: Example: Our family planned a weekend trip to a science museum.

cosy-blockquote.p: Habit – something that you do often and regularly.

p.em: Example: Going to the cinema is a very healthy and fun habit.

cosy-blockquote.p: Health – the state of being free from illness or injury.

p.em: Example: Staying active and visiting friends is good for your mental health.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
According to the article, why is visiting a local museum key to staying active and young?
★ What is the most memorable museum or gallery you have ever visited?

Does the text say that watching plays in a physical theater is better for the mind than TV?
★ Do you prefer watching movies in a physical cinema or streaming them at home?

According to the study, how does culture keep both young ≠ old minds healthy?
★ When was the last time you went to see a live theater performance or play?

How does local culture help us feel less stressed in our daily lives?
★ How do you feel after spending an afternoon surrounded by great art or music?

Why is a creative activity like painting good for relaxing?
★ Do you find that cultural activities help you relax and forget about daily stress?

Does the text show that art can help reduce stress?
★ What is your favorite genre of movie, and does it make you feel younger?

What is the best way to reduce signs of getting old, according to the paper?
★ Who do you usually go with when you attend cultural events?

How does a weekend trip to a gallery compare to a weekend at home for mental energy?
★ Do you think cities should spend more public money on free museums and parks?

How do scientists suggest making museum visits a permanent weekly habit?
★ Have you ever been so moved by a piece of art or performance that you cried?

What changes in our health does the study talk about?
★ What is a cultural custom or event in your town that you love to attend?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: Visual comparison: Watching a blockbuster movie on a small phone screen vs visiting an old theater to see a play. - 📱Phone Screen (Lazy) - 🎭Live Theater (Active)

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
If art helps us live longer, will doctors tell us to go to a museum instead of taking medicine?
★ Would you prefer to learn history through a video game or by visiting a museum?

In the future, will physical theater spaces disappear and be replaced by virtual reality?
★ Do you think virtual reality museums will eventually replace physical gallery visits?

If keeping both young ≠ old brains active is important, should we spend more money on art education?
★ Would you buy a beautiful painting if you knew a computer algorithm had painted it?

If we can live longer by experiencing culture, will humans live past 150 years?
★ Do you think experiencing art should be officially prescribed by doctors for mental health?

In the future, will creative activity be free for older people?
★ Would you enjoy a cinema experience where the plot changes based on your heart rate?

If smart watches can measure our stress, will cities play quiet music to help us relax?
★ Do you think artificial intelligence can ever create art with a genuine human soul?

If visiting a museum can reduce heart strain, should bus trips to museums be completely free?
★ Should admission to all national museums be completely free for everyone?

If a creative trip helps our brain, will travel agencies design holidays to make us smarter?
★ How has your appreciation for movies and theater changed as you have grown older?

If reading is good for the brain, will a daily reading habit be required in all schools?
★ Do you think constant screen time is reducing our interest in live theater?

In the future, will traditional doctor visits be replaced by smart brain scans to protect our health?
★ What historical artist would you spend a day discussing creativity with if you could?

ul.li: Incorrect: I am visit the museum often. → Correct: I visit the museum often. ((Verb conjugation: do not use 'am' before active verbs in simple present tense.))
Incorrect: She no like old theaters. → Correct: She doesn't like old theaters. ((Negation: use 'does not' or 'doesn't' for singular third-person negation in present simple.))
Incorrect: I go to cinema last Sunday. → Correct: I went to the cinema last Sunday. ((Past simple: use the past form 'went' and include the article 'the'.))
